body.statement: For every \(\epsilon>0\), the correspondence \(G_{\epsilon}\) admits a semialgebraic, hence Borel measurable, section \(s_{\epsilon}\) that returns both \(s_{\epsilon}(s)\in\Theta_K\) and an ordered certificate witness, with \(\lVert s_{\epsilon}(s)-s\rVert_w<\inf_{\zeta\in\Theta_K}\lVert\zeta-s\rVert_w+\epsilon\) for every covariance statistic \(s\).
body.justification: This closes the nonattainment gap created by exact rank and strict positive pivots without assuming a nearest model point exists.
body.gap: Brown and Purves treat measurable attained extrema, and Romano and Shaikh invert criteria over identified sets; neither supplies certified approximate projection through this nonclosed exact-rank semialgebraic covariance model.
body.consumer: The augmented confidence construction needs this selector to be measurable and nonempty on every sample, including off-model empirical covariances.
body.proof_tex:
We first verify that the feasible set is nonempty; this is required because an approximate minimizer cannot otherwise be selected.  Let
\[
 a=\frac{m+M}{2},\qquad q=\frac{M-m}{4},\qquad
 Z_0=aI_d,\qquad Z_1=Z_0+q\operatorname{diag}(I_r,0),\qquad Z_e=Z_0\ (e\ge2).
\]
Because \(0<m<M\), all eigenvalues lie in \([m,M]\).  The reference difference has rank \(r\), every later difference has range in its range, and the first \(r\) labels with their natural order have certificate \(L=I_r\), \(D=qI_r\), \(\Lambda_1=qI_r\), and \(\Lambda_e=0\) for \(e\ge2\).  Thus this tuple belongs to \(\Theta_K\).

Next we expose the finite-dimensional real-algebraic structure rather than assuming an attained projection.  Positive semidefiniteness and positive definiteness are finite principal-minor inequalities.  Exact rank \(r\) is expressed by vanishing of all \((r+1)\)-minors and strict positivity of the sum of squares of all \(r\)-minors.  Given exact reference rank \(r\), the common-range condition is expressed by vanishing of all \((r+1)\)-minors of the matrices obtained by adjoining columns of \(Z_e-Z_0\) to \(Z_1-Z_0\).  For each of the finitely many choices of \(T\) and \(t\), the certificate is expressed using real witness variables \(L,D,(\Lambda_e)_e\), the polynomial equations
\[
 Q_{tt}=LDL^{\mathsf T},\qquad
 P_t(Z_e-Z_0)P_t^{\mathsf T}=L\Lambda_eL^{\mathsf T}, \tag{20}
\]
together with unit-lower and diagonal zero equations, strict positivity of the diagonal of \(D\), and nonnegativity of the diagonals of \(\Lambda_e\).  Hence membership in \(\Theta_K\), with one ordered witness retained, is a finite Boolean combination of polynomial equalities and inequalities after existentially eliminating the displayed witness variables.

Let
\[
 v(s)=\inf_{\xi\in\Theta_K}\lVert\xi-s\rVert_w^2.
\]
It is finite because \(\Theta_K\ne\varnothing\).  Its graph is characterized without attainment by
\[
 v\ge0,\qquad
 \bigl(\forall\xi\in\Theta_K\bigr)\ v\le\lVert\xi-s\rVert_w^2,\qquad
 \bigl(\forall u>v\bigr)\bigl(\exists\xi\in\Theta_K\bigr)\
       \lVert\xi-s\rVert_w^2<u. \tag{21}
\]
All expressions in (21) are polynomial after expanding the weighted Frobenius norm.  A cylindrical algebraic decomposition eliminates the quantified coordinates in (20)--(21), so the graph of \(v\) and the augmented graph consisting of
\((s,\zeta,T,t,L,D,(\Lambda_e)_e)\) satisfying (20), \(\zeta\in\Theta_K\), and
\[
 \lVert\zeta-s\rVert_w^2<\bigl(\sqrt{v(s)}+\epsilon\bigr)^2 \tag{22}
\]
are semialgebraic; the square root in (22) is encoded by an auxiliary \(\rho\ge0\) with \(\rho^2=v(s)\).  Every fiber of this augmented graph is nonempty.  Indeed, by the defining property of an infimum, for every \(\epsilon>0\) some \(\zeta\in\Theta_K\) has \(\lVert\zeta-s\rVert_w<\sqrt{v(s)}+\epsilon\), and membership supplies one of the finitely many ordered witnesses.

It remains to justify the section asserted by \(\text{def:certified-approximate-selector}\).  In the fixed cylindrical decomposition, order the finitely many cells.  Over each base cell choose the first cell having a nonempty fiber.  A cylindrical cell in one new coordinate is either the graph of one of its semialgebraic boundary functions or a band between two such functions.  Select the boundary value in the graph case, the midpoint for two finite boundaries, the lower boundary plus one or the upper boundary minus one for a one-sided band, and zero for a two-sided unbounded band.  Repeating this coordinate by coordinate produces a semialgebraic point in the chosen fiber.  Induction over the finitely many coordinates gives a semialgebraic section of the augmented graph, including the discrete ordered-certificate branch.  Its covariance component is the map \(s_{\epsilon}\).

By construction,
\[
 s_{\epsilon}(s)\in\Theta_K,\qquad
 \lVert s_{\epsilon}(s)-s\rVert_w
 <\inf_{\xi\in\Theta_K}\lVert\xi-s\rVert_w+\epsilon, \tag{23}
\]
and the retained variables satisfy (20), hence certify the returned tuple.  Finally, a semialgebraic map is Borel measurable: the inverse image of an open coordinate box is the projection of its semialgebraic graph intersected with that box, hence is semialgebraic by the same cylindrical elimination, and coordinate boxes generate the Euclidean Borel sigma-field.  This proves all parts of the lemma without assuming that the infimum in (21) is attained.
